i have about 5k sitting in my schwab account, will the bot use all of it?

No. It only uses up to the real-money cap you set in Setup (your plan is $50), whatever else is in the account. Its checkbook only holds the money and positions it opened itself, so it never touches your other cash or stocks. Before buying it also checks the cash the broker says is available and spends the smaller amount. Kestrel treats Schwab as a cash account, so it only spends settled money there.

got a popup saying the bot was updated but this window wasnt, what do i do

It means macOS didn't let the app replace itself in Applications (it has no paid Apple developer ID). The bot's own code was updated, so trading already uses the new version; only the window is older. To let the window update too, go to System Settings → Privacy & Security → App Management and turn Kestrel on. The alert's Open App Management button takes you there. Or press Download and drag the new version into Applications. Later just closes the message.

how much does pushover cost

The Pushover app is free for 30 days, then a one-time $4.99 per platform (iPhone/iPad, Android or Desktop). Sending is free up to 10,000 messages a month. Setup's step 5 tag shows how many Kestrel has sent this month out of 10,000, and near that limit only urgent alerts go out. If you'd rather not use Pushover, Telegram also delivers alerts, and Telegram is the only way to send Kestrel commands from your phone.

explain tjr strategy in simple terms

The idea: big moves often start with a fake-out. Price drops just below an obvious low, which triggers other traders' stop-losses, then turns around and breaks back up. Kestrel waits for that whole sequence on 5-minute bars: hourly trend up, a dip below yesterday's low or a recent swing low, then a close above the last swing high. It buys on the pullback into the price gap the move left, only from 9:35 to 11:30am, with a stop just under the dip and a target of 2 times the risk.

what's opening_range_breakout

A day-desk method. The first 30 minutes after the open set the day's opening range, and it has no opinion while that range forms. After that, it buys if the price breaks above the range's high and exits if the price falls back below the middle of the range. Like every day trade, anything still open is sold 10 minutes before the close.

when does the swing desk actually make its trades?

Once a day, 15 minutes before the close: 3:45pm New York time on a normal day, 12:45pm on early-close days. That's when it scores its stocks and places buys and sells. The rest of the trading day the autopilot still checks the swing positions every 5 minutes, but only for stop-losses. It decides near the close because its backtest decides and fills at each day's close, and the same code runs in testing, paper and live, so what was tested is what trades.

how far below the buy price are the stops?

Swing desk: a fixed 7% below what it paid, the stop it was tested with. Day desk: half the stock's usual daily range (its 14-day average true range), at least 1% and at most 5%; if the range is unknown, 2%. A wider stop buys a smaller position: no day trade loses more than 0.66% of the desk at its stop, and no position is bigger than 33% of the desk. Honest note: sizing stops to volatility is a common rule of thumb, not a tested edge.

wheres the setting that stops it buying right before earnings

It's Don't buy right before earnings (swing desk) in Setup → Settings. On (skip the last 3 trading days) means the swing desk won't open a new position within 3 trading days of a company's earnings report, because a report can jump a stock 10-20% overnight, past its stop. What it already owns is kept. Dates come from Yahoo each morning. The honest trade-off: stocks have on average done slightly better around earnings, so this gives up a little of that for fewer big surprise losses. Pick Off to disable it.

what's the kill switch and the daily loss limit?

They're two automatic brakes on each desk. Daily loss limit: if a desk is down 3% on the day, it makes no new buys that day. Kill switch: if a desk falls 15% below its best day, it triggers an emergency stop that sells everything that desk owns and halts it; a live desk then drops back to paper. If you set up Pushover, a real-money kill switch or emergency stop alert repeats every minute until you open it.

what if the mac goes to sleep while the bot owns stocks

There are backups, though staying awake is the dependable setup. Every real position has a stop-loss order resting at the broker. When the Mac wakes, the day desk sells any leftovers the moment it can, since it never means to hold overnight. If the swing desk missed its daily decision, the Journal flags it. With lid-closed mode on, a weekday 8:30am New York time wake-up is also set, but wake-ups with the lid closed aren't guaranteed.

why did the swing desk sell something

One of four things: the 7% stop-loss was hit; momentum's score fell below 0.5, meaning the stock dropped out of the top half of its ranking; the stock fell below its 200-day average (its score goes to 0); or it was a trim because one stock grew to more than twice its 12.5% share. Every sale has its reason written next to it in the Activity list and the journal, so you can see which one it was. The market falling below its 200-day average doesn't force sales; it just stops new buys.

which brokers does kestrel treat as cash accounts?

With the account type on auto: Schwab and Webull are treated as cash accounts, so only settled money is spent. That's the safe assumption; if your account is really margin, these rules only cost a day's wait. Alpaca is treated as margin: every Alpaca account is a margin type, and Alpaca covers unsettled money itself, so there are no good faith violations there. You can set the account type in Setup → Settings. Kestrel never borrows either way.

how does the swing desk decide what to buy

Right now (Stage 1) it uses momentum. At 3:45pm it lines up every stock it's considering, its watchlist plus up to 30 strong, affordable names from the daily scan, and ranks them by how much they rose over the past 12 months, leaving out the latest month. A stock in the top 20% that's also above its 200-day average is a buy, strongest first, while there are free slots (8 in total) and cash. If SPY itself is under its 200-day average, it holds what it has and buys nothing new.

how do i stop the bot right now

It depends what you want. To stop new trades but keep what it owns, press Pause at the top of the window and confirm; stop-losses keep working. To get out completely, press Emergency stop, type SELL EVERYTHING and press Sell everything and stop: it cancels the bot's orders, sells everything it owns and halts both desks. From your phone, send /pause or /kill SELL EVERYTHING to your Telegram bot. To switch off the background autopilot itself, use Setup → 2. Autopilot → Turn off.

how do i turn off fractional shares

Setup → Real money, Schwab, Webull and Claude (for later) → Settings → Fractional shares (Alpaca and the simulation) → Off: whole shares only, then press Save settings. With it on, the bot can buy parts of a share at Alpaca and in the simulation, at least $1 at a time, only for stocks Alpaca allows. Schwab and Webull are whole shares only either way, so pricey stocks are skipped there. A stock whose single share costs more than a position's budget gets a "too pricey" tag on the watchlist.

is the demo using my real account? will it mess anything up

No. Demo data lives in its own folder (data/demo) and your real data is never touched. The prices are made up (a random walk), and the banner says "Not your account." The Setup screen keeps working on your real setup even while the demo is showing. Turn the demo off with View → Show Demo Data again.

how do i turn on the autopilot

Open Setup and go to step 2, Autopilot, then press Turn on. It runs the bot in the background: it starts when you log in and restarts itself if it stops. The tag next to Autopilot shows on, off, or "on · not running", and a "Last problem" line appears if it stopped recently. The pill at the top of the window shows "Autopilot running" and when it last checked in. Keep the Mac plugged in, and turn on lid-closed mode just below if you want to close the lid.

what has to happen before kestrel can trade my real money?

Four locks all have to be open, and each desk (swing and day) earns it separately. 1) The desk's paper results pass the promotion rules: at least 30 trading days of paper trading, it made money, it beat SPY over the same days, and it never dropped more than 10% from its best day. 2) Your ~/AITrader/.env file says LIVE_TRADING_ENABLED=true. 3) Prices are real-time, meaning Alpaca or Schwab data, not free Yahoo data. 4) You run the promote step and type REAL MONEY exactly. If any one is missing, no real order goes out.

does kestrel update itself or do i have to download every new version

It updates itself. While the app is open (it can sit minimized), it checks its download page when it opens and once a day. When there's a newer version it downloads it, checks the download's fingerprint and signature, swaps itself and restarts, and a running background autopilot restarts on the new version. With paper trading only, this happens automatically. If real money is involved, it asks you first. It must be in your Applications folder to replace itself. Versions before 1.0.13 can't update themselves: download the zip once more by hand.

is paper trading realistic or does it look better than real life?

Close, but not perfect. Alpaca's paper fills are simplified, with no market impact or slippage, so paper looks a bit better than reality; that's one reason real money starts small. The simulation on your Mac fills every order 0.05% worse than the quote to stay honest. Keep the paper amount equal to your real-money cap so paper behaves like your real account. And 30 paper days is a small sample: passing is evidence, not proof.

what tags does it record on a buy

The stock itself ('buying NIO'). A stock under $5. On the day desk: whether it was a stock in play or from the fixed list, and whether it was bought in the first 30 minutes or after 2pm. Chasing: on the day desk, already up 3% or more since the open; on the swing desk, up 10% or more in 5 days. Moving with a stock it already owns. And option bets against it. These tags are what the mistake memory groups trades by.

can kestrel text me when it buys or sells something

Yes. Set up Telegram in Setup step 5 and your private Kestrel bot messages you every buy and sell, with what it spent, what it got back and whether it was a win or a loss, plus the after-close results, the after-market report and anything urgent like a pause or the kill switch. If you'd rather have push notifications, add Pushover in the same step; it sends every buy and sell too. You can use both. The Mac sends them, so it needs to be awake and online.

my mac was on wifi all day but it didnt trade, why

Being on Wi-Fi isn't enough by itself: the Mac also has to be awake with the autopilot running. Most often a MacBook fell asleep because the lid was closed, which sleeps it unless lid-closed mode is on and it's plugged in. Check the pill at the top of the window: "Autopilot off" or "Autopilot last seen ... min ago" means it wasn't checking in. Turn the autopilot on in Setup step 2, plug in, and turn on Keep trading with the lid closed if you close the lid. The Journal flags a missed swing decision.
